subject: Cherry-pick [2.7] Fix hierarchical FL startup failures: deployment timeouts, selective client exclusion, and dead-detection debounce (#4209) (#4288)
message:
Cherry-pick [2.7] Fix hierarchical FL startup failures: deployment timeouts, selective client exclusion, and dead-detection debounce (#4209) (#4288)

## Problem

Large-scale hierarchical FL jobs (e.g. BERT NER, 144 clients, 6 relays
on Frontier) abort in
Round 0 due to a cascading startup failure chain.  The root sequence is:

1. F3 streaming HOL stall (PR #4206) delays deployment ACKs from
relay-connected clients
2. **`_deploy_job()`** treats `reply=None` (timeout) as `"unknown"` —
not a failure — so
   timed-out clients silently appear to have been deployed
3. **`_start_run()`** tries to start those clients; they again time out,
and
   `check_client_replies()` ignores the `None` reply
4. **`_sync_client_jobs()`** fires dead-job notification on the very
first heartbeat with
   no startup grace period
5. FedAvg requires 144/144 — one or two missing clients → abort
6. A late-starting CJ crashes with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not
iterable` when
`get_job_clients()` receives `None` metadata from an already-aborted job

PRs #4206, #4204, #4174, #4172, #4186, #4211, #4210 (all merged in
2.7.2) address the
transport layer.  This PR addresses the remaining job lifecycle layer.

---

## Fixes Included

### 1 — `_deploy_job()`: Treat deployment timeout as failure
(`job_runner.py`)

**Root bug**: `reply=None` was logged as `"unknown"` and excluded from
`failed_clients`,
so timed-out clients counted as "successfully deployed" for the
`min_sites` check.

**Fix**: Add timed-out clients to `failed_clients` with a `"deployment
timeout"` label.
The existing `min_sites` / `required_sites` logic then correctly decides
whether to abort.

### 2 — `check_client_replies()`: Return timed-out clients instead of
raising (`admin.py`)

**Root bug**: In strict mode, any timeout raised immediately, aborting
the whole job even
when the remaining active clients satisfied `min_sites`.

**Fix**: In strict mode, collect timed-out clients into a return list
rather than raising.
Explicit errors (non-OK return code or error body) still raise. Also
fixes the non-strict
mode to use name-keyed dict lookup instead of fragile positional
`zip()`.

New signature: `check_client_replies(...) -> List[str]` (timed-out
client names; empty = none).

### 3 — `_start_run()`: Selective exclusion with min_sites re-evaluation
(`job_runner.py`)

**Root bug**: A start-job timeout under strict mode aborted the entire
job with no
tolerance for stragglers within `min_sites` bounds.

**Fix**: Use the returned timed-out list from `check_client_replies()`.
If remaining
active clients >= `min_sites`, log a warning and proceed. Only abort
when below tolerance.

### 4 — `_sync_client_jobs()`: Require-prior-report default changed to
`True` (`fed_server.py`)

**Root bug**: `SYNC_CLIENT_JOBS_REQUIRE_PREVIOUS_REPORT` defaulted to
`False`, meaning
the bug fix was opt-in and the unsafe behaviour remained the default.

**Fix**: Default changed to `True`. Operators who want the aggressive
legacy detection
can set it to `False` explicitly.

### 5 — `_sync_client_jobs()`: Move `_reported_clients` out of
`job_info` dict (`fed_server.py`)

**Root bug**: Positive-observation tracking was stored as
`job_info["_reported_clients"]`,
injecting algorithm state into a data dict with no corresponding
`RunProcessKey` constant.

**Fix**: Tracking moved to `self._job_reported_clients: Dict[str, set]`
on `FederatedServer`.
Stale entries are purged whenever a job is no longer in `run_processes`.

### 6 — `ClientRunManager.get_job_clients()`: Explicit meta validation
(`client_run_manager.py`)

Raises `RuntimeError` with a descriptive message instead of an opaque
`TypeError` when
`JOB_CLIENTS` is absent or the wrong type.

---

## Configuration Recommendations (No Code Change Needed)

| Setting | Recommended value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `FedAvg(min_clients=...)` | 96-98% of `num_clients` | Tolerates a few
startup stragglers |
| `runner_sync_timeout` | `120` s | Allows Lustre-backed deployments
time to complete |
| `strict_start_job_reply_check` | `true` | Start-job timeouts surfaced,
straggler clients excluded |
| `sync_client_jobs_require_previous_report` | `true` (now the default)
| Prevents premature dead-job from startup delay | |
`SFM_CLOSE_STALLED_CONNECTION` (PR #4206) | `true` after staging |
Disconnects stalled relay connections |

---

## Files Changed

- `nvflare/private/fed/server/job_runner.py` — `_deploy_job()` timeout
as failure; `_start_run()` selective exclusion
- `nvflare/private/fed/server/admin.py` — `check_client_replies()`
returns timed-out list; dict-keyed non-strict path
- `nvflare/private/fed/server/fed_server.py` — `_sync_client_jobs()`
default `True`; `_job_reported_clients` attr; stale cleanup
- `nvflare/private/fed/client/client_run_manager.py` — explicit meta
validation in `get_job_clients()`

---

## Test Coverage

New and updated unit tests with both positive and negative cases:

| File | Tests | What they cover |
|---|---|---|
| `admin_test.py` | 8 | Timeout returned not raised; dict lookup; error
still raises; reorder OK |
| `job_runner_test.py` | 4 | strict flag wiring; timeout within
tolerance → warn; timeout below tolerance → raise | |
`job_runner_deploy_test.py` | 9 (new file) | Timeout counted as failure;
OK reply not failed; mixed outcomes; detail label; min_sites with
timeouts; integration sequence |
| `fed_server_test.py` | 5 | Default requires-prior-report; legacy
explicit-False still fires; tracking in server attr not job_info; stale
cleanup |

All 29 targeted unit tests pass.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for each changed function (positive + negative)

classification end-to-end
- [x] All 29 targeted unit tests pass

subject: Qwen-VL LoRA Support (#4277)
message:
Qwen-VL LoRA Support (#4277)

Fixes # .

### Description

# Qwen3-VL example: LoRA training fixes

## Summary
This PR makes the Qwen3-VL NVFlare example self-contained and stabilizes
both full-model and LoRA federated training paths.

Key outcomes:
- Removes dependency on cloning external Qwen repos by vendoring
required `qwenvl` train/data code.
- Fixes LoRA adapter-only FL training failures (`trainable params: 0`,
empty optimizer groups, grad_fn/backward issues).
- Improves runtime behavior by using in-memory parameter exchange for
default single-process runs.
- Keeps checkpoint-based exchange for multi-rank runs, with optimized
adapter artifact handling.

## Changes

### 1) Self-contained Qwen3-VL example
- Vendored `qwenvl/train/*` and `qwenvl/data/*` into the example.
- Removed external patch/repo dependency path and updated docs/NOTICE.

### 2) LoRA training correctness
- In adapter-dir load path (`train_qwen.py`), explicitly enables LoRA
params for training.
- Ensures PEFT path runs in train mode and avoids
gradient-checkpointing/PEFT backward failures.
- Uses PEFT-aware optimizer construction with trainable params only.

### 3) Single-process in-memory exchange
- For default `WORLD_SIZE=1`, client no longer relies on checkpoint
round-trip between receive/train/send.
- Loads received FL params into model in-process and returns trained
params directly from memory.

### 4) Multi-rank path performance and safety

subject: Cherry-pick [2.7] Client-side memory management  (#4211) (#4290)
message:
Cherry-pick [2.7] Client-side memory management  (#4211) (#4290)

This PR aligns the 2.7 branch with allocator-aware **client-side memory
management** capabilities and recipe-level configurability,
complementing server-side memory controls.

In long-running FL workloads, client processes can accumulate memory
over rounds due to:
- delayed Python garbage collection release
- allocator behavior (glibc arena retention vs jemalloc decay)
- PyTorch CUDA cache retention

This is amplified for:
- large models and long jobs
- constrained edge environments
- Swarm-like topologies where clients can have higher memory pressure

1. **Allocator Detection**: `get_allocator_type()` detects active
allocator at runtime
   - glibc: uses `malloc_trim()` path
   - jemalloc: uses decay behavior (`MALLOC_CONF`)

2. **Transparent Integration**: cleanup is triggered after
`flare.send()`; user training scripts require no code changes

3. **Configurable Frequency**:
- Recipe-side: `client_memory_gc_rounds` (PT/TF/base) or
`memory_gc_rounds` (Swarm)
   - ScriptRunner-side: `memory_gc_rounds`
   - `0` = disabled, `1` = every round, `N` = every N rounds

4. **GPU Support**: `cuda_empty_cache=True` triggers CUDA cache cleanup
(PyTorch only)

5. **Subprocess Support**: external process settings propagate via:
   - `NVFLARE_CLIENT_MEMORY_GC_ROUNDS`
   - `NVFLARE_CUDA_EMPTY_CACHE`
   - plus allocator env (`MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`, `MALLOC_CONF`)

6. **jemalloc Startup Integration (Opt-in)**: startup template preloads
jemalloc only when `NVFLARE_ENABLE_JEMALLOC_PRELOAD=true`, and sets
recommended `MALLOC_CONF`

```python
from nvflare.app_opt.pt.recipes import FedAvgRecipe

recipe = FedAvgRecipe(
    min_clients=2,
    num_rounds=100,
    train_script="client.py",
    client_memory_gc_rounds=5,
    cuda_empty_cache=True,
)
```

```python
from nvflare.app_opt.pt.recipes.swarm import SimpleSwarmLearningRecipe

recipe = SimpleSwarmLearningRecipe(
    name="my_swarm",
    model=MyModel(),
    num_rounds=100,
    train_script="client.py",
    memory_gc_rounds=5,
    cuda_empty_cache=True,
)
```

```python
executor = ScriptRunner(
    script="train.py",
    memory_gc_rounds=5,
    cuda_empty_cache=True,
)
```

> Note: these are workload-dependent estimates; profile your deployment
for exact numbers.

| Operation | Typical Duration | Notes |
|-----------|------------------|-------|
| `gc.collect()` | 10-500 ms | depends on object graph | |
`malloc_trim()` (glibc) | < 1 ms | typically very fast | |
`torch.cuda.empty_cache()` | < 50 ms | can synchronize CUDA stream |

For round durations in seconds/minutes, cleanup overhead is typically
small.

| Scenario | `server_memory_gc_rounds` | `client_memory_gc_rounds` |
`cuda_empty_cache` | Notes |


|----------|---------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Quick experiments | 0 | 0 | False | minimal overhead | | Standard
training | 5 | 5-10 | False | balanced | | Long training (100+ rounds) |
5 | 5 | True | prevent gradual growth | | Large models (10B+ params) |
1-3 | 1-3 | True | aggressive cleanup | | Memory-constrained edge | 5 |
1 | True | maximize stability |

- **PyTorch**: FedAvg, FedAvg-HE, FedEval, FedOpt, Scaffold, Cyclic,
Swarm
- **TensorFlow**: FedAvg, FedOpt, Scaffold, Cyclic
- **NumPy / classic workflows**: FedAvg, Cross-Site Eval, LR FedAvg
- **Base recipes**: `nvflare/recipe/fedavg.py`,
`nvflare/recipe/cyclic.py`

TF recipes do **not** expose `cuda_empty_cache`.
`torch.cuda.empty_cache()` is PyTorch-only; TF GPU memory is managed
differently. TF subclasses hard-code `cuda_empty_cache=False` to the
parent/ScriptRunner. The parameter will be added back when TF-specific
GPU cache cleanup is implemented.

In swarm learning both the trainer role and the aggregator role run on
the client. The old code unconditionally called `gc.collect()` after
each trainer submission in `Gatherer.gather()`. This PR replaces that
with:
- configurable per-FL-round cadence via `memory_gc_rounds` (default `1`
= every round, preserving legacy behavior)
- full `cleanup_memory()` call (`gc.collect` + `malloc_trim` + optional
CUDA) instead of bare `gc.collect`, giving allocator-aware OS-level
memory return
- `cuda_empty_cache` wired through since the aggregator client may also
hold GPU tensors from training

The parameter is named `memory_gc_rounds` (not
`client_memory_gc_rounds`) in `SimpleSwarmLearningRecipe` because both
roles are client-side.

Documentation was updated to clarify Swarm uses `memory_gc_rounds` and
`cuda_empty_cache` as top-level recipe args (not `train_args`).

| Recipe | Reason |
|--------|--------|
| Sklearn | Small models; Python GC has negligible impact | | XGBoost |
C++-managed memory; Python GC not impactful | | FedEval |
Evaluation-only, single-pass |
| server `cuda_empty_cache` | Servers typically have no GPU | | TF
`cuda_empty_cache` | PyTorch-only; TF cleanup not yet implemented |

- config key: `ConfigKey.CUDA_EMPTY_CACHE`
- env var: `NVFLARE_CUDA_EMPTY_CACHE`

subject: Cherry-pick [2.7] Pass-Through: Zero Tensor Copy at CJ for Large-Model Federated Training (#4210) (#4289)
message:
Cherry-pick [2.7] Pass-Through: Zero Tensor Copy at CJ for Large-Model Federated Training (#4210) (#4289)

This PR introduces the **pass-through architecture** for
`ClientAPILauncherExecutor`, eliminating tensor materialisation at the
CJ (Client Job) process when large models are exchanged between the FL
server and a subprocess agent.

In large-model federated learning (e.g., 7B–70B LLM fine-tuning), the CJ
process today acts as a blind relay that fully deserializes and
re-serializes every tensor it receives from the FL server before
forwarding to the subprocess. For a 70B float16 model, this consumes
~140 GB of CJ memory and requires two complete network transfers. B1
pass-through removes both costs.

---

NVFlare's multi-hop execution path for `launch_external_process=True`
looks like:

```
FL Server ──serialize──▶ CJ process ──re-serialize──▶ Subprocess agent
```

Each tensor in the global model is handled as follows at CJ:

1. **Server** serializes the model and creates a download transaction
(tensor data lives on the server).
2. **CJ** fully *downloads* every tensor from the server into its own
heap, materialising the complete model in CJ memory.
3. **CJ** re-serializes the model for the subprocess, creating a *new*
download transaction — the subprocess then downloads from CJ.

For large models, this means:
- **CJ peak memory = full model size** (potentially 100s of GB).
- **Two full network transfers**: server → CJ, then CJ → subprocess.
- **CJ becomes a throughput bottleneck** and an OOM risk for any model
that doesn't fit in the CJ process's memory.

This is the reason why workflows are infeasible for large models beyond
what the CJ machine can hold.

---

With `FOBSContextKey.PASS_THROUGH` enabled on CJ's cell FOBS context,
the data path becomes:

```
FL Server ──stream──▶ CJ (LazyDownloadRef only, no tensor data)
                          └──forward ref──▶ Subprocess
                                               └──download──▶ FL Server
```

CJ holds **only lightweight placeholders** (< 100 bytes per tensor). The
subprocess downloads each tensor directly from the FL server — CJ is
never involved in the tensor data path.

(`nvflare/fuel/utils/fobs/__init__.py`)
A new context key that signals ViaDownloaderDecomposer to skip the
download step and create lazy placeholders instead.

A small sentinel object (four fields: `fqcn`, `ref_id`, `item_id`,
`dot`) created by `recompose()` in PASS_THROUGH mode. It carries the
original FL server's FQCN, batch ref_id, intra-batch item ID, and Datum
Object Type — everything the subprocess needs to download the tensor
directly.

A named sentinel stored in `fobs_ctx[items_key]` during PASS_THROUGH
receive. Using a typed class (rather than a plain tuple) makes the
PASS_THROUGH branch unambiguous and immune to accidental type collisions
with real item dicts.

A new auto-registered FOBS decomposer for `LazyDownloadRef`. When CJ
re-serializes a task containing `LazyDownloadRef` objects:

- **`decompose()`** delegates to `get_dot_handler(lazy.dot)` — the
original `ViaDownloaderDecomposer` subclass (e.g., `TensorDecomposer`,
`NumpyArrayDecomposer`). That handler's `_finalize_lazy_batch`
post-callback re-emits the *original* server datum (fqcn + ref_id + DOT)
so the subprocess knows exactly where to download from. `lazy_dot` is
appended to the encoding dict for routing on the receive side.
- **`recompose()`** uses `lazy_dot` to look up the handler and delegates
to `handler.recompose()`, which retrieves the real tensor from
`fobs_ctx[handler.items_key]` (populated by `process_datum()` when the
subprocess received the forwarded datum).

The `dot` (Datum Object Type) field on both `LazyDownloadRef` and
`_LazyBatchInfo` ensures that numpy arrays stay with
`NumpyArrayDecomposer` and PyTorch tensors stay with `TensorDecomposer`,
preserving type safety through the full pass-through hop.

(`client_api_launcher_executor.py`)
On startup, the executor enables PASS_THROUGH on the engine cell's FOBS
context:

```python
cell.core_cell.update_fobs_context({FOBSContextKey.PASS_THROUGH: True})
```

This single line activates the full B1 architecture for every job that
uses `launch_external_process=True` — including `llm_hf` and any recipe
that calls `ScriptRunner(launch_external_process=True)`.

---

The pipe (CellPipe) operates on already-serialized bytes. Intercepting
at the pipe level would require parsing FOBS binary format, re-writing
datum references, and re-assembling the byte stream — fragile and
tightly coupled to the wire format.

Intercepting at the FOBS decomposer level is the natural extension
point: decomposers already control exactly when and how data is
materialised. PASS_THROUGH simply adds a "don't materialise" branch to
that existing mechanism.

The subprocess must know *which* `ViaDownloaderDecomposer` subclass owns
the downloaded data so it can store it in the correct
`fobs_ctx[items_key]` and route `recompose()` correctly. The `dot`
field, set when the server originally serialized the tensor, carries
this type information through the pass-through hop without any
type-switching logic.

| Stage | Before (tensor materialised) | After (B1 pass-through) |
|-------|------------------------------|------------------------| | CJ
receive | Full model size (e.g., 140 GB) | ~100 bytes per tensor | | CJ
forward | Creates new download tx | Re-emits original server datum |
| Subprocess receive | Downloads from CJ | Downloads directly from FL
server |

---

1. **Zero tensor copy at CJ** — CJ memory footprint is independent of
model size.
2. **One network transfer** instead of two — tensors travel server →
subprocess directly.
3. **No CJ OOM risk** for large models regardless of CJ machine memory
capacity.
4. **Transparent to job authors** — no changes to job configs, training
scripts, or recipe APIs; `launch_external_process=True` automatically
activates B1.
5. **Type-safe** — `dot` propagation preserves tensor type (numpy /
pytorch) through the hop without any if/elif type switching.

---

- All existing jobs using `launch_external_process=True` automatically
benefit. No config or script changes required.
- Jobs using `launch_external_process=False` (in-process executor) are
completely unaffected — `ClientAPILauncherExecutor.initialize()` is not
called.
- For models smaller than the ViaDownloaderDecomposer streaming
threshold (2 MB per array), FOBS uses native (inline) serialization
regardless of `PASS_THROUGH` — behaviour is identical to before.
- `LazyDownloadRefDecomposer` is auto-registered via the existing
`register_folder` mechanism; no explicit registration call is needed by
any caller.

---

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `nvflare/fuel/utils/fobs/__init__.py` | Add
`FOBSContextKey.PASS_THROUGH` |
| `nvflare/fuel/utils/fobs/decomposers/via_downloader.py` | Add
`LazyDownloadRef`, `_LazyBatchInfo`, PASS_THROUGH branches in
`process_datum()` / `recompose()`, `LazyDownloadRefDecomposer`,
`_finalize_lazy_batch` post-callback |
| `nvflare/app_common/executors/client_api_launcher_executor.py` |
`initialize()` enables PASS_THROUGH on engine cell |

Cherry-pick [2.7] Fix recipe API bug list and harden recipe behavior (#4228) (#4293)

## Issues addressed
This PR addresses the reported recipe bug list:

- `BUG-8` (Critical): `CyclicRecipe` `model=None + initial_ckpt` created
phantom persistor reference and runtime failure.
- `BUG-1` (Critical): `CyclicRecipe` dict model config caused
`TypeError`.
- `BUG-7` (Critical): base `CyclicRecipe` silently ignored
`initial_ckpt`.
- `BUG-9` (High): `FedAvgRecipe` `per_site_config[\"server\"]` caused
invalid target handling/crash.
- `BUG-4` (High): `Recipe.execute/export` mutated job state and made
recipe reuse unsafe.
- `BUG-2` (Medium): `FedAvgRecipe` per-site `or` fallback ignored falsy
overrides.
- `BUG-3` (Medium): `SimEnv` with `num_clients=0` and client list
resolved `num_threads=0`.
- `BUG-5` (Low): base `FedAvgRecipe` accepted `initial_ckpt` +
`model=None` but produced incomplete model source.
- `BUG-6` (Low): `add_cross_site_evaluation` idempotency guard depended
only on transient `_cse_added` attribute.

## Changes
- Hardened base `CyclicRecipe` model/persistor setup:
  - fail-fast when a valid persistor cannot be configured;
  - support dict model config for supported frameworks;
- apply/validate `initial_ckpt` for wrapper and framework-specific
paths.
- Hardened base `FedAvgRecipe`:
- validate and reject reserved `per_site_config` targets (`server`,
`@ALL`);
- preserve falsy per-site override values via explicit `is not None`
fallback;
  - fail-fast when no persistor and no model params are available.
- Added shared framework persistor setup utility in recipe utils and
wired both Cyclic/FedAvg paths to it.
- Made `Recipe.execute()` and `Recipe.export()` reusable-safe by
snapshot/restore of temporary execution params.
- Fixed `SimEnv` default resolution for `num_clients`/`num_threads` when
explicit client list is provided.
- Hardened CSE idempotency with workflow-based detection in addition to
`_cse_added` fast-path.
- Updated impacted examples and exports:

subject: fix(dashboard): harden mass-assignment  (#4343)

fix(dashboard): harden mass-assignment  (#4343)

## Summary

- Replace unrestricted `setattr` mass-assignment with field allowlists
in all patch methods (user, client, project), blocking
`role_id`/`password_hash`/`root_key` writes
- Block denied users (`approval_state < 0`) at login
- Add `approved` claim to JWT; gate data-listing endpoints on approval
so pending users cannot enumerate users/clients
- Require authentication on `GET /project` and `GET /organizations`
- Remove creator-side client org reassignment
- Harden `serialize_pri_key`: raise `TypeError` on non-bytes passphrase
instead of silently falling through to `NoEncryption()`
- Add 7 security regression tests (6 of 7 fail against pre-fix code, all
pass post-fix)

## Known limitation

Stateless JWTs have a 30-minute lifetime. If a user is denied after
token issuance, their existing token remains valid until expiry. The
`approved` claim + endpoint gating covers the normal case; the login
check covers the denied case for new tokens.

subject: fix: use safe deserialization for torch.load and np.load (#4344)
message:
fix: use safe deserialization for torch.load and np.load (#4344)

## Summary

- Add `weights_only=True` to all unsafe `torch.load()` calls in
`ditto.py` (lines 77, 84) to prevent arbitrary code execution via pickle
deserialization (CVE-2025-32434 / CWE-502)
- Change default of `load_weights_only` parameter in
`PTFileModelPersistor.__init__` from `False` to `True` so the safe path
is the default
- Add `allow_pickle=False` to all unsafe `np.load()` calls across four
files to prevent pickle-based arbitrary code execution (CWE-502)
- Replace `random.sample` with `secrets.choice` in `generate_password()`
in `lighter/utils.py` to use a cryptographically secure RNG (CWE-338)

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `nvflare/app_opt/pt/ditto.py` | `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`
on lines 77 and 84 |
| `nvflare/app_opt/pt/file_model_persistor.py` | `load_weights_only:
bool = True` (default changed) |
| `nvflare/app_common/ccwf/comps/np_file_model_persistor.py` |
`np.load(..., allow_pickle=False)` |
| `nvflare/app_common/ccwf/comps/np_trainer.py` | `np.load(...,
allow_pickle=False)` |
| `nvflare/app_common/np/utils.py` | `np.load(..., allow_pickle=False)`
(two call sites) |
| `nvflare/app_common/np/np_trainer.py` | `np.load(...,
allow_pickle=False)` |
| `nvflare/lighter/utils.py` | `secrets.choice` replaces `random.sample`
|

## Security impact

- **CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)**: `torch.load` without
`weights_only=True` and `np.load` without `allow_pickle=False` both
allow arbitrary Python object deserialization, enabling remote code
execution if an attacker can supply a malicious model file. These fixes
restrict loading to safe tensor/array primitives only.
- **CVE-2025-32434**: Directly addressed by `weights_only=True` on all
`torch.load` call sites.
- **CWE-338 (Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG)**: `random.sample` uses
a non-cryptographic RNG seeded from system time, making generated
passwords predictable. `secrets.choice` uses OS-level CSPRNG.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `torch.load` calls in `ditto.py` still load `.pt` files
correctly (model state dicts contain only tensors and primitives —
compatible with `weights_only=True`)
- [ ] Verify `PTFileModelPersistor` loads standard checkpoint files
without error with the new default
- [ ] Verify numpy `.npy` files (non-pickled arrays) load correctly with
`allow_pickle=False`
- [ ] Verify `generate_password()` still returns a 16-character
alphanumeric string
- [ ] Run existing unit tests: `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/ -v`

subject: Add deterministic repo Markdown relative-link check (#4339)
message:
Add deterministic repo Markdown relative-link check (#4339)

## Summary
- add a deterministic repo-local relative link checker for tracked
`*.md` files across the repository
- run it in GitHub Actions on pull requests that touch Markdown or the
checker itself
- add focused unit coverage for fenced code, `file:///` examples, and
HTML `src` handling
- fix the current stale repo-local Markdown links needed for the new
check to pass on `main`

## Why
The previous network-based link checker was removed in #4104 and
cherry-picked in #4106 after repeated timeout and ignore-list
maintenance on external sites. This PR adds back coverage for the
specific class of regression that recently slipped through: broken local
relative links caused by repo path changes.

## Why This Is More Robust Than The Old Link Check
The old workflow relied on network requests to external websites. That
made it vulnerable to slow or flaky servers, growing ignore lists, and
CI failures unrelated to repository changes.

This PR is more robust because it:
- checks only repository-local relative links, so results do not depend
on network availability or third-party uptime
- resolves links from the source file location, which directly targets
moved or renamed in-repo paths
- ignores fenced code and literal `file:///` examples, which avoids
false positives from documentation snippets
- runs against all tracked Markdown files in the repository, so moved or
renamed docs outside `examples/advanced` are caught too

## Scope
This workflow intentionally checks tracked repository Markdown files
only (`git ls-files '*.md'`). It does not validate external URLs,
generated dashboard HTML assets, or notebook Markdown yet, which keeps
the check stable and avoids the flaky timeout behavior that led to the
old workflow being removed.

## Verification

subject: Cache model and data across FL rounds in hello-flower examples (#4372)
message:
Cache model and data across FL rounds in hello-flower examples (#4372)

Closes #3834
              
  ## Summary
The hello-flower examples load model and dataset at module level,
causing them to be reloaded on every FL round when
NVFlare re-imports the module. This adds ~40s overhead compared to pure
Flower (~130s vs ~90s as reported in the
issue).
## Fix
Replace eager module-level loading with a lazy `_ensure_data_loaded()`
function called from `client_fn()`. Data and
model are loaded once on the first round and cached in module-level
globals for all subsequent rounds.
  Applied to both:
- `examples/hello-world/hello-flower/flwr-pt/flwr_pt/client.py`
- `examples/hello-world/hello-flower/flwr-pt-tb/flwr_pt_tb/client.py`
                                                                       
## Before
  ```python
# Loaded at import time — reloaded every round
net = Net().to(DEVICE)
  trainloader, testloader = load_data()
  After
net = None
  trainloader = None
  testloader = None

def _ensure_data_loaded():
      global net, trainloader, testloader
if net is None:
net = Net().to(DEVICE)
      if trainloader is None or testloader is None:
          trainloader, testloader = load_data()

def client_fn(context):
      _ensure_data_loaded()
      ...

subject: Preserve CURRENT_ROUND context attrs in BaseModelController (#4384)
message:
Preserve CURRENT_ROUND context attrs in BaseModelController (#4384)

## Summary
Preserve the existing `FLContext` property attributes when
`BaseModelController` updates `CURRENT_ROUND` during result processing.

This removes the warning seen in recipe-based FedAvg examples such as
`examples/hello-world/hello-tf`:

```text
property 'current_round' already exists with attributes private:sticky, cannot change to private:non-sticky
```

## Root Cause
`CURRENT_ROUND` handling on `main` drifted into an inconsistent state
across two earlier changes:

- `#4226` added callback-context round propagation in
`BaseModelController._process_result()`, but always wrote
`CURRENT_ROUND` as `private=True, sticky=True`.
- `#4329` later updated `FedAvg` to keep `CURRENT_ROUND` and
`NUM_ROUNDS` as non-sticky in the workflow context.

Once both changes were present, recipe-based FedAvg workflows could
populate `CURRENT_ROUND` as non-sticky and then hit the
attribute-mismatch warning when contribution callbacks reused the same
`FLContext`.

There is also closely related prior work in closed `2.7` PR `#4220`
(`[2.7] Fix CURRENT_ROUND context in ModelController contribution
events`). This PR applies the same attribute-preservation idea to `main`
in the current code layout.

## Changes
- Add a small helper in `BaseModelController` to reuse the existing
`private/sticky` attributes when a context property already exists.
- Use that helper in `_process_result()` when populating callback
`CURRENT_ROUND`.
- Reuse the same helper in `set_fl_context()` for `CURRENT_ROUND` and
`NUM_ROUNDS` so the behavior stays consistent.
- Add a regression test covering the non-sticky FedAvg path and
asserting that no warning is emitted.

## Validation
- `pytest tests/unit_test/app_common/workflow/fedavg_test.py -q`
- `black --check nvflare/app_common/workflows/base_model_controller.py
tests/unit_test/app_common/workflow/fedavg_test.py`
- `isort --check-only --profile black
nvflare/app_common/workflows/base_model_controller.py
tests/unit_test/app_common/workflow/fedavg_test.py`

does not change aggregation math or task acceptance behavior.

subject: fix: create optimizer once instead of every batch in edge training (#4377)
message:
fix: create optimizer once instead of every batch in edge training (#4377)

Addresses item #5 in #3827

## Summary

The SGD optimizer in `ETTaskProcessor.run_training()` was being
recreated on every batch iteration. This discards accumulated momentum
state between steps, which degrades model convergence when momentum,
weight decay, or Nesterov acceleration are configured.

**Before:** optimizer created inside the inner batch loop — momentum
resets every step, effectively making `momentum=0` regardless of config.

**After:** optimizer created once before the first step and reused
across all batches and epochs, preserving stateful internals (momentum
buffers, dampening, etc.) throughout training.

This is a correctness fix — the previous behavior silently produced
suboptimal training results for any non-zero momentum configuration.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run edge training example with `momentum > 0` and verify loss
curve improves vs. previous behavior
- [ ] Run `./runtest.sh -s` to verify style checks pass
- [ ] Verify no regressions in existing edge training tests

subject: Add distributed provisioning: nvflare cert/package CLI + runtime security fixes (#4380)
message:
Add distributed provisioning: nvflare cert/package CLI + runtime security fixes (#4380)

## Summary

Implements distributed provisioning for NVFlare — an inverted-trust
workflow where each
site generates its own RSA private key locally. Only CSRs are exchanged
out-of-band; the
Project Admin never handles any site private key. The produced startup
kits are structurally
identical to centrally provisioned kits at runtime.

## New CLI Commands

- **`nvflare cert init`** — Project Admin bootstraps the root CA
(one-time per federation).
  Produces `rootCA.pem`, `rootCA.key` (0600), `ca.json`.
- **`nvflare cert csr`** — Site Admin generates RSA key + CSR locally.
Types: `client`,
`server`, `org_admin`, `lead`, `member`. Private key never leaves the
machine.
- **`nvflare cert sign`** — Project Admin signs a received CSR with the
root CA. The `-t`
type arg is authoritative — CSR role field is ignored (prevents
privilege escalation).
- **`nvflare package`** — Site Admin assembles a startup kit from their
local key + the
signed cert + rootCA.pem received from the Project Admin. Supports
`--dir` auto-discovery
  or explicit `--cert/--key/--rootca` paths.

All commands support `--output json` (machine-readable), `--output
quiet`, and `--schema`
(prints JSON schema for the command and exits).

## Runtime Security Fixes

| Fix | File | Change |
|-----|------|--------|
| D1 | `lighter/impl/signature.py` | Stop generating `signature.json`
for non-CC, non-HE kits — mTLS is the trust anchor for plain kits |
| D2 | `fed/utils/fed_utils.py` | Gate startup integrity check on
`valid_config` (not just `secure_train`) — prevents false abort when
`signature.json` is absent |
| D3 | `fed/server/job_runner.py`, `fed/client/training_cmds.py`,
`hub/hub_app_deployer.py`, `fed/server/job_cmds.py` | Job signature
verification now checks `__nvfl_sig.json` presence +
`require_signed_jobs` policy instead of `secure_train`; strips
`FROM_HUB_SITE` from user-submitted job meta to prevent privilege
escalation |
| D4 | `fuel/hci/client/file_transfer.py` | Guard `push_folder` signing
behind key-file existence check — simulator mode no longer errors on
missing key |
| D5 | `fuel/hci/client/config.py` | `secure_load_admin_config` allows
`NOT_SIGNED` when `valid_config=False` — admin login works for manual
workflow and non-CC kits |
| D6 | `fed/server/job_runner.py` | Add
`_require_signed_jobs(workspace)` helper: reads `fed_server.json`,
defaults to `True` when `rootCA.pem` present |

## New Infrastructure

- `nvflare/tool/cli_output.py` — `output()` / `output_error()` with
json/quiet/human-readable rendering
- `nvflare/tool/cli_errors.py` — centralized error code registry with
template messages and hints
- `nvflare/tool/cli_schema.py` — `parser_to_schema()` generates JSON
schema from argparse definitions

## Test Coverage

215 unit tests added across 12 new test files. All pass.

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/tool/ -v` — CLI + cert +
package (186 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest
tests/unit_test/lighter/test_signature_builder.py -v` — D1 (7 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/fuel/hci/client/ -v` — D4 + D5
(13 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/private/fed/ -v` — D2 + D3 + D6
(9 + 8 + 21 + 9 tests)
- [ ] Manual workflow: `cert init` → `cert csr` → `cert sign` →
`package` → site start
- [ ] Verify simulator still works (no `signature.json`, no
`require_signed_jobs` enforcement)
- [ ] Verify CC kit startup check still runs (regression)

subject: [codex] Handle run-state polling connection teardown (#4420)
message:
[codex] Handle run-state polling connection teardown (#4420)

## Summary
- tolerate transient `ConnectionError` and `SessionClosed` while the
integration harness polls run state
- keep `_get_run_state()` from failing the test during normal
server/admin teardown

## Root Cause
PR #4400 migrated the integration harness from the deprecated
`FLAdminAPI` surface to `flare_api.Session`.

With the new session path, `get_job_meta()` and `show_stats()` can raise
real exceptions during teardown when the server side is already
disconnecting. `_get_run_state()` already handled `JobNotFound` and
`JobNotRunning`, but it did not handle the transient connection/session
teardown exceptions, so the `np_app` integration case could fail
sporadically with `ConnectionError: cannot connect to server:
APIStatus.ERROR_SERVER_CONNECTION`.

## Why This Fix
The run-state polling loop should treat transient teardown disconnects
like the already-handled end-of-run races: skip that poll iteration and
continue. The change is intentionally narrow and only catches the
connectivity/session exceptions that are expected during teardown.

## Validation
- reproduced the failure locally on a synthetic merge snapshot of PR
#4415 into `main`
- validated that `np_job` passed on the same synthetic merge snapshot
- reran the reproduced `np_app` integration case locally 10 times on the
same synthetic merge snapshot after the fix: 10/10 passed

subject: Add heterogeneous-rank HLoRA enhancement to MedGemma example (#4424)
message:
Add heterogeneous-rank HLoRA enhancement to MedGemma example (#4424)

## Summary

This draft PR extends the advanced MedGemma example with a
heterogeneous-rank HLoRA workflow on top of the merged federated
fine-tuning example.

Changes introduced:
- add fixed-global-rank custom LoRA aggregators for both the paper
baseline (`naive`) and HLoRA (`hlora`)
- keep the stock FedAvg controller path while making the client
rank-aware: each site truncates the server LoRA bank to its local rank
before local training
- support heterogeneous local ranks from `job.py`, with distinct ranks
used by default for the 3-client example
- update data preparation to default to a more heterogeneous
label-skewed client split and emit a client label-distribution SVG for
visualization
- add per-site runtime and peak CUDA memory logging in the client
- add `--finetune_only` to `run_evaluation.py` for faster repeated
checkpoint comparisons
- update the MedGemma README with the heterogeneous-rank workflow and
observed comparison results

## Observed comparison

Using the heterogeneous-rank 3-client layout (`4,8,16`) on
`CRC-VAL-HE-7K`:

| Run | Naive | HLoRA | Delta |
|------|-------|-------|-------|
| default seed | `0.8955` (`6430/7180`) | `0.9414` (`6759/7180`) |
`+0.0458` |
| alternate seed | `0.8961` (`6434/7180`) | `0.9366` (`6725/7180`) |
`+0.0405` |

## Notes

- This PR intentionally keeps the standard controller path and
introduces the HLoRA logic through custom aggregators plus a rank-aware
client.
- The custom `naive` aggregator remains necessary in the
heterogeneous-rank setting because plain built-in FedAvg tensor
averaging is not shape-safe once sites use different LoRA ranks.

subject: Add PyTorch param validation for model exchange (#4392)
message:
Add PyTorch param validation for model exchange (#4392)

## Summary

This change adds fail-fast parameter-contract validation to NVFlare's
PyTorch model exchange and persistence paths, so key and shape drift
becomes explicit instead of being silently skipped.

The same validation now applies consistently to both native PyTorch and
PyTorch Lightning clients.

## What changed

- add `inspect_model_params` and `ModelParamMatchReport` in
`nvflare.app_opt.pt.utils`
- make `feed_vars()` raise on zero-match and shape mismatch, and warn on
unexpected incoming keys
- make `PTModelPersistenceFormatManager.update()` reject persistence
updates that would introduce unexpected keys or mismatched shapes
- reuse the same validation in the PyTorch Lightning callback before
`load_state_dict()`
- in Lightning `strict=True`, reject unexpected keys before calling
`load_state_dict()`
- in Lightning `strict=False`, warn, filter to matched keys, and
preserve missing-key diagnostics for partial loads
- keep the new code and tests compatible with Python 3.8
- add focused unit coverage for native PyTorch and Lightning mismatch
paths

## Why

This is aimed at failures like wrapper-induced key drift such as
`model.*` vs. unwrapped names, where the current path can silently
ignore loads or save mixed keyspaces. The new validation makes those
failures visible immediately and gives enough context to diagnose the
mismatch.

## Before and after

Before this change, an incoming payload like `["model.fc.weight",
"model.fc.bias"]` sent to a model expecting `["fc.weight", "fc.bias"]`
could be silently skipped by the load path and later merged into
persistence as a mixed keyspace.

After this change, the same mismatch fails fast with a diagnostic like:

```text
None of the 2 incoming model parameter(s) matched the local model's 2 parameter(s). Incoming keys: 2 sample=['model.fc.bias', 'model.fc.weight']. Local keys: 2 sample=['fc.bias', 'fc.weight']. Unexpected keys sample: ['model.fc.bias', 'model.fc.weight']. Hint: stripping common prefix 'model.' would match 2/2 incoming key(s).
```

subject: fix: read epoch count from training config in simulation mode (#4404)
message:
fix: read epoch count from training config in simulation mode (#4404)

Addresses item #4 in #3827

## Summary

`ETTaskProcessor.process_task()` calls `run_training()` without passing
`total_epochs`, so simulation mode always trains for exactly 1 epoch
regardless of the epoch value in `training_config`. This means simulated
devices behave differently from real devices, which read the epoch count
from `device_training_params`.

**Before:** `run_training(et_model)` — always 1 epoch, ignoring config.

**After:** `run_training(et_model,
total_epochs=self.training_config.get("epoch", 1))` — reads epoch from
training config, defaults to 1 to preserve existing behavior.

### Changes

1. **`et_task_processor.py`** — add `"epoch"` to default
`training_config` (default: 1), read it in `process_task()` and pass to
`run_training()`. Validate at init time using `check_positive_int`
(consistent with `EdgeJob`, `BaseState`, etc.) so that `epoch=0` or
`epoch="three"` fails fast instead of silently skipping training or
crashing in `calc_params_diff`.

2. **`et_job.py`** — add `"epoch": 3` to both CIFAR-10 and XOR task
processor configs so simulation matches `device_training_params`.

3. **`et_task_processor_test.py`** (new) — 14 unit tests covering:
   - Default epoch config, override, preservation of other defaults
- Rejection of non-positive values (0, -1, -10) and non-integer types
(1.5, str, None)
- `run_training` respects `total_epochs` for 1 and 3 epochs (verified
via forward_backward call counts)
   - `process_task` reads epoch from `training_config`
   - Helper functions `clone_params` and `calc_params_diff`

subject: Add missing edge web model types to FOBS type whitelist (#4444)
message:
Add missing edge web model types to FOBS type whitelist (#4444)

## Summary

PR #4295 introduced a FOBS `type_name` whitelist to prevent RCE via
deserialization, and PR #4298 added some missing types. However, **12
edge web model types** from `nvflare.edge.web.models.*` were not
included in the whitelist.

When edge external-device workflows run, FOBS deserialization fails on
child nodes with:
```
Type 'nvflare.edge.web.models.device_info.DeviceInfo' is not allowed.
Use fobs.register_data_classes(), fobs.register_enum_types(),
or fobs.add_type_name_whitelist() to allow this type.
```

This causes edge jobs to hang in `RUNNING` status indefinitely because
child nodes cannot process edge messages.

## Root Cause

- **Worked in**: 2.7.2rc12 (before whitelist was introduced)
- **Broken since**: 2.7.2rc15 (first build containing PR #4295 and
#4298)
- The `BUILTIN_TYPES` set in `builtin_decomposers.py` was missing all
edge web model types that flow through F3/cell message passing

## Fix

Added all 12 edge web model types to `BUILTIN_TYPES`:
- `DeviceInfo`, `UserInfo`, `Capabilities`
- `JobRequest`, `JobResponse`
- `TaskRequest`, `TaskResponse`
- `SelectionRequest`, `SelectionResponse`
- `ResultReport`, `ResultResponse`
- `ErrorResponse`

## Test Plan

- [x] `L0_edge_num_async_job_ext` test passes (previously failed
consistently since 2.7.2rc15)
- [x] Verified on both Python 3.10 and 3.12
- [x] All other L0 edge tests continue to pass

subject: fix(android): convert recursive fetchTask/fetchJob retries to a loop (#4416)
message:
fix(android): convert recursive fetchTask/fetchJob retries to a loop (#4416)

Both `fetchTask` and `fetchJob` in the Android SDK call themselves
recursively when the server returns RETRY. `suspend fun` + `withContext`
doesn't get tail-call optimized on the JVM, so every retry adds a real
stack frame.

Under synchronous FedAvg an Android device with a smaller dataset
finishes its round before the server is ready to hand out the next task.
The server sends RETRY with short `retryWait` values (30ms observed in
#3827). A few thousand retries exhaust the Android main thread stack
(~1MB) and the app crashes with a StackOverflowError.

This converts both methods to iterate with `while(true)`. On OK, return
via `return@withContext`. On RETRY, delay and loop. On errors, throw.
The request body is rebuilt inside the loop so cookies from a prior
RETRY response carry forward to the next attempt. `delay()` still honors
coroutine cancellation and `IOException` still aborts the sequence.

Verified by reproducing the control flow in a standalone Kotlin file and
running 10,000 back-to-back RETRY iterations without a stack overflow.

Fixes item #12 in #3827.

subject: Add docker job launcher (#4409)
message:
Add docker job launcher (#4409)

### Description

Enables container-based job execution for NVFlare sites that have Docker
but no Kubernetes.

Current PR scope: this PR uses `DockerLauncherBuilder` in central
`project.yml` so Docker launcher support is usable immediately.

Intended future architecture: launcher selection should move to a
localized post-provision site configuration step shared by Docker and
K8s rather than staying in centralized provisioning. That shared
two-step workflow is follow-up work and not part of this PR.

**New components**

- `DockerJobLauncher` (`ClientDockerJobLauncher` /
`ServerDockerJobLauncher`): launches SJ/CJ as Docker containers per job.
Docker SDK imported lazily via `try/except` at module level so SJ/CJ
containers (which load `resources.json` but never call Docker APIs)
don't require the SDK.
- `DockerLauncherBuilder`: provisioning builder that generates
`start_docker.sh` per site and replaces the site's default job launcher
in `resources.json` so exactly one launcher is configured.
- `start_docker.sh` template: starts SP/CP container with Docker socket
mounted, workspace bind-mounted, and `NVFL_DOCKER_WORKSPACE` set. Runs
as `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` so workspace files are owned by the
calling user. Adds `--group-add $(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)`
(portable Linux/macOS) so the container process can reach the Docker
daemon. Removes stale `daemon_pid.fl` before each start (Docker
containers always run as PID 1).

**Job configuration**

All Docker-mode configuration lives in `meta.json`. `deploy_map` is
launcher-agnostic (same plain `app → [sites]` format as process mode).
All Docker-specific config moves to `resource_spec`:

```json
{
  "deploy_map": {"app": ["server", "site-1", "site-2"]},
  "resource_spec": {
    "server": {
      "docker": {"image": "nvflare-job:latest"}
    },
    "site-1": {
      "docker": {"image": "nvflare-job:latest", "num_of_gpus": 1, "shm_size": "8g"},
      "process": {"num_of_gpus": 1}
    }
  }
}
```

A job may carry resource entries for multiple launcher modes for
portability across deployments, but the active launcher is chosen only
by the site's configured launcher in `resources.json`.

- `resource_spec[site][docker]`: image, GPU count, and any additional
`docker run` flags (Docker SDK naming). Missing image for a
Docker-configured site is a hard error at `launch_job` time — no silent
fallback to process mode.
- `resource_spec[site][process]`: process-mode resource spec (unchanged
from before).
- `num_of_gpus` in `docker` spec is translated to `device_requests`
internally. Explicit `device_requests` takes precedence.
- Site-level defaults via `default_job_container_kwargs` in
`resources.json`; job-level `resource_spec[site][docker]` wins on
conflict.
- Legacy flat `resource_spec[site] = {"num_of_gpus": N}` (no mode
nesting) treated as process mode for backward compatibility.
- Study data mount: `local/study_data.json` maps study name → host data
path; mounted read-only at `/var/tmp/nvflare/data` in SJ/CJ. Re-read on
every job launch — no SP/CP restart needed.

**Networking**

- SP/CP and SJ/CJ containers share a Docker bridge network
(`nvflare-network`) for intra-site parent↔child communication.
Cross-site (CP→SP) uses the published `fed_learn_port` over HTTPS/gRPC,
identical to process mode.
- `PARENT_URL` overridden at launch time to use the SP/CP container name
so job containers connect back via Docker DNS.
- Internal listener always bound to `0.0.0.0` so SJ/CJ containers can
reach the parent via Docker DNS.

**Container environment (SJ/CJ)**

- `working_dir` set to workspace mount so relative paths in job scripts
resolve inside the workspace.
- `USER` and `HOME` injected so libraries calling `getpass.getuser()` or
`os.path.expanduser()` don't crash when the host UID has no
`/etc/passwd` entry in the container.
- `PYTHONPATH` set to job custom dir (job-level BYOC) + site custom dir
(`workspace/local/custom/`, site-level BYOC) — same priority as process
mode.
- Job containers run as same UID:GID as SP/CP so all workspace files are
readable/writable by the parent process.

**Other fixes and changes**

- `extract_job_image`: removed — launcher selection no longer depends on
image presence. Launcher choice now comes from site configuration in
`resources.json`; missing Docker image fails at `launch_job` time.
- `get_launcher_resource_spec`: new utility that handles mode-nested
`resource_spec` with legacy flat fallback.
- `JobMetaValidator`: `deploy_map` entries now only allow `{sites,
targets}` — image and container_kwargs have moved to `resource_spec`.
- `NVFL_P_IMAGE` env var: override SP/CP image at runtime without
re-provisioning.
- Removed `run_in_docker` per-participant flag — all sites provisioned
with `DockerLauncherBuilder` always get `start_docker.sh` and the
`0.0.0.0` listener binding.
- `DockerLauncherBuilder` validates `admin_port == fed_learn_port` at
provision time (server container only publishes one port); the default
provisioning already satisfies this.
- Docker client validated lazily on first job launch (not at init) so
the component loads cleanly in SJ/CJ containers that don't have Docker
access.

subject: Distributed provisioning, job CLI connection args, system commands, and parity tests (#4462)
message:
Distributed provisioning, job CLI connection args, system commands, and parity tests (#4462)

## Summary

This PR completes the distributed provisioning feature and CLI
enhancements, fixing several correctness issues found during review and
testing.

---

### CLI fixes
    - replace -"-out-format json" to -"-format json "
    -     


### Distributed provisioning workflow (`nvflare cert` + `nvflare
package`)

Implements the full manual provisioning workflow so that private keys
never leave each site:

| Step | Command |
|------|---------|
| Project Admin (once) | `nvflare cert init --project <name> -o
<ca-dir>` |
| Site Admin | `nvflare cert csr -n <name> -t <type> -o <csr-dir>` |
| Project Admin | `nvflare cert sign -r <name>.csr -c <ca-dir> -o
<out-dir> --accept-csr-role` |
| Site Admin | `nvflare package -e grpc://<server>:<port> --dir
<bundle-dir>` |

`nvflare package` supports three modes: directory (`--dir`),
project-file (`-p site.yaml`), and explicit (`--cert/--key/--rootca`).
Kit type is derived automatically from the signed certificate; no `-t`
needed.

### Package builder pipeline fix

The YAML-mode builder assembly was stripping `WorkspaceBuilder` and
`StaticFileBuilder` from `site.yaml` and ignoring their custom args,
contradicting the design doc's claim that site.yaml "supports custom
builders." Fixed to:
- Honor `WorkspaceBuilder` and `StaticFileBuilder` from YAML as-is (with
custom args preserved)
- Replace `CertBuilder` in YAML with `PrebuiltCertBuilder` (the only
intentional substitution)
- Inject defaults only when the corresponding builder is absent from
YAML

### `nvflare job` — connection args on all subcommands

`--startup-kit` and `--startup-target` (the admin startup kit selector)
were previously only available on `nvflare job submit`. They are now
available on every job subcommand:

```
nvflare job list --startup-kit /path/to/admin/startup
nvflare job list --startup-target prod
nvflare job meta <job-id> --startup-target prod
nvflare job abort <job-id> --startup-kit /path/to/admin
nvflare job logs <job-id> --startup-target poc
```

All subcommands affected: `list`, `meta`, `abort`, `clone`, `delete`,
`download`, `stats`, `logs`, `monitor`, `log-config`.

### `nvflare job` — export fixes

Three bugs in the job export workflow fixed:

1. **`--export` / `--export-dir` unrecognized arguments**: `job.py` uses
argparse before `execute()` runs, so `--export`/`--export-dir` were
rejected. Fixed by stripping these flags from `sys.argv` at
`recipe/spec.py` import time via `_consume_recipe_args()`.

2. **"Job folder not valid" on re-export**: Partial exports leave
directories without `meta.json`, causing a `RuntimeError` on the second
run. Fixed by always `rmtree`-ing the output directory if it exists.

3. **`NoneType` error after export**: `execute()` returned `None` after
exporting; fixed to `raise SystemExit(0)` so callers do not attempt to
use the return value.

### `nvflare system` command extensions

- **`shutdown` / `restart`**: Extended to support all three targets
(`server`, `client`, `all`) with optional positional `client_names`,
matching the original admin console.
- **`remove-client`**: New command wrapping `Session.remove_client()`.
- **`InvalidTarget` error**: Was incorrectly reported as
`CONNECTION_FAILED`; now correctly exits with `INVALID_ARGS` (exit 4).

### `_server_status_value` regression fix

`check_status` and `Session.shutdown_system()` were reading
`engine.server.status` (process machine state) instead of
`engine.get_engine_info().status.value` (FL engine state). This caused
incorrect status reporting.

### Examples and docs

- `examples/advanced/distributed_provision/interactive_mode/README.md`:
added copy-and-run shell examples for all four steps
- `docs/design/distributed_provisioning.md`: updated to reflect final
design decisions
- `docs/user_guide/nvflare_cli/system_command.rst`: document all three
shutdown/restart targets, add Remove Client section

---

## Test plan

- [ ] `TestDistributedProvisioningWorkflow` (16 tests): end-to-end cert
init → csr → sign → package; file structure, permissions, JSON config
consistency
- [ ] `TestKitParity` (10 tests): centralized (`nvflare provision`) and
distributed kits produce identical file sets, JSON key structures, and
endpoint values; cert/key content differs (different CAs)
- [ ] `TestYamlModeBuilderPipeline` (6 tests): YAML
WorkspaceBuilder/StaticFileBuilder honored, CertBuilder replaced,
defaults injected only when absent, ordering correct
- [ ] `TestSessionShutdown` / `TestSessionRestart` (16 tests): all
target types and client_names combinations
- [ ] `TestSystemShutdown` / `TestSystemRestart` /
`TestSystemRemoveClient`: CLI command dispatch and error handling
- [ ] Job connection args: `--startup-kit` / `--startup-target` present
on all job subcommands (list, meta, abort, clone, delete, download,
stats, logs, monitor, log-config)
- [ ] Job export tests: `--export` flag consumed before argparse,
re-export does not raise, `SystemExit(0)` after export
- [ ] Integration test files renamed `test_xxx.py` → `xxx_test.py`
(project convention)

subject: Handle quoted admin submit_job paths (#4456)
message:
Handle quoted admin submit_job paths (#4456)

## Summary
- make HCI command parsing honor shell-style quoting for admin commands
such as `submit_job`
- keep a legacy whitespace-splitting fallback for malformed quoting to
avoid new parse failures
- add focused unit tests for quoted job paths and existing `#`
command-props behavior

## Why
Dragging a job folder into the admin console on Ubuntu can produce a
single-quoted path. The current parser only switches to `shlex.split()`
when a command contains double quotes, so single-quoted paths are passed
through literally and `submit_job` rejects the resulting folder path.

## Root Cause
`nvflare.fuel.hci.cmd_arg_utils.split_to_args()` and
`parse_command_line()` special-case double quotes instead of using
shell-like tokenization generally. That leaves single quotes in the
parsed argument, which then flows into the client-side file transfer
path lookup.

## Impact
This change allows quoted drag-and-drop job paths to be submitted from
the admin console without manually stripping surrounding quotes.

Fixes #1328.

subject: Optimize SVTPrivacy memory usage (#4459)
message:
Optimize SVTPrivacy memory usage (#4459)

## What changed

This updates `SVTPrivacy` to avoid flattening the entire model into a
single temporary vector and then allocating multiple same-size helper
arrays on top of it.

The new implementation:
- processes parameters in fixed-size chunks instead of concatenating the
full model
- tracks accepted entries with compact boolean masks rather than a
global candidate index array
- repartitions the final sample across tensors/chunks without
materializing the full accepted-index list
- preserves upstream scalar passthrough behavior while still counting
scalar entries toward `size(ΔW)` when computing the upload budget
- adds focused unit tests for no-replacement selection counts,
zero-fraction behavior, replacement-mode shape safety, and scalar-budget
accounting

## Why it changed

`SVTPrivacy` was prone to large transient allocations. For bigger
models, the original implementation could eagerly create:
- one full flattened `delta_w`
- one full clipped copy
- one full `candidate_idx` index array
- one or more additional noise/index temporaries during selection

That causes memory usage to spike well beyond the model size itself and
can trigger OOMs on models that are otherwise feasible to train.

## Impact

This keeps the same SVT-style mechanism while substantially reducing
peak memory and improving runtime.

In isolated subprocess benchmarks on synthetic float32 models, the
refactor reduced filter-induced peak RSS by about 70% to 82%:

- 1M params, low share: 195.3 MiB -> 47.2 MiB extra peak RSS (75.8%
reduction)
- 2M params, low share: 371.8 MiB -> 90.8 MiB (75.6% reduction)
- 4M params, low share: 679.6 MiB -> 145.4 MiB (78.6% reduction)
- 4M params, multi-tensor low share: 709.5 MiB -> 128.0 MiB (82.0%
reduction)
- 4M params, high share: 691.2 MiB -> 203.2 MiB (70.6% reduction)
- 4M params, multi-tensor high share: 710.0 MiB -> 183.2 MiB (74.2%
reduction)

The same runs were also faster with the chunked implementation.

## Root cause

The OOM risk came from whole-model temporary allocations inside
`SVTPrivacy`, not from the underlying model alone. A moderately large
update could expand into several additional full-size arrays and Python
index containers during the selection loop.

## Validation

### Focused tests

- `pytest tests/unit_test/app_common/filters -q`
  - result: `9 passed`

### Statistical parity checks

Compared the new implementation with `upstream/main` on synthetic
single-tensor, multi-tensor, chunked, and scalar-edge models across
multiple hyperparameter settings.

After fixing scalar budget accounting, the refactor stayed statistically
aligned with upstream:
- mean shifts in `nonzero_count`, `L1`, `L2`, and `mean_abs_nonzero`
stayed below about 0.25% in the tested settings
- mean-difference z-scores stayed below 1.5
- coordinate selection-frequency differences were comparable to or
smaller than upstream-vs-upstream Monte Carlo noise baselines

## Notes

This PR intentionally does not preserve exact seed-for-seed numerical
equality with the old implementation for multi-tensor/chunked inputs,
because the refactor changes how randomness is consumed across chunks.
The goal here is distributional parity with much lower memory overhead,
and the validation above supports that.

subject: Add launcher_spec to job meta (#4464)
message:
Add launcher_spec to job meta (#4464)

### Description

## Summary

Adopt the `launcher_spec`-based job metadata model for launcher-specific
runtime configuration, while preserving backward compatibility with the
existing `resource_spec` contract.

This PR moves Docker and K8s launcher-specific fields such as `image`,
`shm_size`, and K8s `cpu`/`memory` out of overloaded `resource_spec`
semantics and into a dedicated top-level `launcher_spec` section. Shared
scheduler-facing resource requirements such as `num_of_gpus` remain in
`resource_spec`.

## What Changed

### Job metadata / validation
- Added top-level `launcher_spec` support in job metadata.
- Added server-side validation for `launcher_spec` structure and allowed
launcher modes.
- Kept existing `resource_spec` validation intact.

### Launcher resolution utilities
- Added `get_job_launcher_spec(job_meta, site_name, mode)`.
- Resolution behavior:
1. merge `launcher_spec["default"][mode]` with
`launcher_spec[site][mode]`
  2. site-specific values win
3. fall back to nested `resource_spec[site][mode]` for backward
compatibility

### Docker launcher
- Docker job image is now read from
`launcher_spec[site]["docker"]["image"]`.
- Docker-specific runtime flags are read from
`launcher_spec[site]["docker"]`.
- `num_of_gpus` still falls back to flat `resource_spec[site]` for
backward compatibility.
- Existing site-level defaults in `default_job_container_kwargs` /
`default_job_env` continue to work.

### K8s launcher
- K8s job image is now read from `launcher_spec[site]["k8s"]["image"]`.
- K8s launcher now consumes `cpu` / `memory` from
`launcher_spec[site]["k8s"]`.
- GPU remains sourced from `resource_spec[site]["num_of_gpus"]`.
- `handle_event(BEFORE_JOB_LAUNCH)` registers the K8s launcher
unconditionally, consistent with site-policy launcher selection. If
required K8s job config such as `image` is missing, `launch_job()` fails
with a clear error.


### Docs
Updated design docs to match the current implementation:
- `docs/design/job_meta_launcher_config.md`
- `docs/design/JobLauncher_and_JobHandle.md`
- `docs/design/Docker_Job_Launcher_Design.md`
- `docs/design/helm_chart_design.md`

The docs now consistently describe:
- `launcher_spec` as the launcher-facing config section
- `resource_spec` as the scheduler/resource-facing section
- `default` merge behavior
- current Docker and K8s launcher behavior
- Helm/K8s image sourcing via `launcher_spec`

## Backward Compatibility

This change is intended to be backward compatible with existing
`2.7.2`-style jobs:

- existing flat `resource_spec[site]` continues to work for
scheduler-facing resource requirements
- nested `resource_spec[site][mode]` remains supported as a
compatibility fallback
- new jobs should prefer `launcher_spec` for launcher-specific fields

## Recommended Job Metadata Shape

```json
{
  "deploy_map": { "app": ["@ALL"] },
  "resource_spec": {
    "site-1": { "num_of_gpus": 2, "mem_per_gpu_in_GiB": 16 }
  },
  "launcher_spec": {
    "default": {
      "docker": { "image": "repo/nvflare:2.7.2" },
      "k8s": { "image": "repo/nvflare:2.7.2" }
    },
    "site-1": {
      "docker": { "shm_size": "8g" },
      "k8s": { "cpu": "500m", "memory": "2Gi" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Why
This gives us:

- clear separation of concerns
- better naming and semantics
- no duplication of shared resource fields
- cleaner validation boundaries
- a path to support richer launcher-specific config without overloading
resource_spec

### Testing
Updated unit tests for launcher spec resolution and launcher behavior.
Added/updated Docker and K8s launcher tests for launcher_spec handling
and backward compatibility.

subject: Fix JobRunner completion context race (#4471)
message:
Fix JobRunner completion context race (#4471)

## Summary
This PR fixes a server-side race in JobRunner when completed jobs are
processed concurrently with scheduling.

The completion thread was reusing the scheduling loop's FLContext, and
both paths mutate FLContextKey.CURRENT_JOB_ID. Under concurrent jobs,
that could fire JOB_COMPLETED with the wrong job id, leaving completed
jobs stuck in DefaultJobScheduler.scheduled_jobs and blocking later jobs
from being scheduled.

## Changes
- pass engine into the completion thread instead of the shared FLContext
- create a fresh engine.new_context() for each completed job before
firing JOB_COMPLETED
- add a regression test covering completion-event context isolation

## Validation
- tests/unit_test/private/fed/server/job_runner_test.py

subject: K8s launcher: use CellNet workspace transfer instead of a shared workspace PVC (#4469)
message:
K8s launcher: use CellNet workspace transfer instead of a shared workspace PVC (#4469)

This PR updates the Kubernetes job launcher to run launched jobs without
mounting the shared workspace PVC.

Instead, launched jobs now:
- mount `startup/` from a Secret
- use an `emptyDir` as their writable workspace
- download `local/` and the job workspace over CellNet/F3 before startup
- upload job results back to the parent over the same path on shutdown

This preserves `local/` workspace behavior while isolating each launched
job's writable workspace.

subject: feat: add live job log streaming (#4454)
message:
feat: add live job log streaming (#4454)

## Summary
- Adds **JobLogStreamer** (client) and **JobLogReceiver** (server) for
real-time log streaming from clients to the server during federated
jobs, replacing the deprecated `ErrorLogSender`/`LogReceiver` which only
sent static snapshots after job completion.
- Adds **SystemLogStreamer** — a system-level widget for
`resources.json` that automatically injects `JobLogStreamer` into jobs
that don't already declare one, by modifying the deployed
`config_fed_client.json` at `BEFORE_JOB_LAUNCH`.
- Updates provisioning templates: client uses `SystemLogStreamer`
(streams `error_log.txt`), server uses `JobLogReceiver`.
- Includes `hello-log-streaming` example and unit tests.

### Why streaming runs inside the job, not in CLIENT_PARENT
The streamer must run inside the job subprocess rather than being
managed from the parent process. With Docker or Kubernetes job
launchers, the job may run in a different container or pod that the
parent process has no filesystem access to. Streaming from CLIENT_PARENT
would only work with the local process launcher. By injecting
`JobLogStreamer` into the job config, the streamer always runs where the
log file lives — regardless of the launch mechanism.

### Key design points
- `LogStreamer` tails growing log files, survives log rotation, and
sends liveness heartbeats so the receiver can detect dead senders via
idle timeout.
- `JobLogStreamer` uses a two-phase stop: `ABOUT_TO_END_RUN` sets
`stop_event` only (returns immediately so framework log lines land in
the file during the drain window); `END_RUN` joins the thread to keep
`client_run()` alive until EOF is acknowledged.
- A fresh `Signal` is injected into the streaming `FLContext` via
`put()` (not `set_prop()`) to bypass the mask-consistency check that
would otherwise leave the triggered `run_abort_signal` in place.
- `JobLogReceiver` writes chunks directly to a file as they arrive so
the log can be followed with `tail -f`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `examples/hello-world/hello-log-streaming/job.py` in simulator
— verify streamed log matches original
- [ ] Run with POC mode — verify `SystemLogStreamer` injects
`JobLogStreamer` into jobs without one
- [ ] Verify `ALLOW_ERROR_SENDING=false` in project.yml removes
`SystemLogStreamer` from provisioned `resources.json`
- [ ] Run unit tests: `pytest
tests/unit_test/app_common/streamers/log_streamer_test.py`

subject: Multi-study CLI: runtime study management commands and registry (#4472)
message:
Multi-study CLI: runtime study management commands and registry (#4472)

## Problem

NVFlare's multi-study support was provisioning-only: studies had to be
defined in `project.yml`
before provisioning and could not be modified at runtime. Operators
needed to reprovision and
restart the server to enroll new sites, add users, or register new
studies — impractical for
long-running federated deployments.

## Solution

This PR introduces the `nvflare study` CLI command group — 8 subcommands
for runtime lifecycle
management of studies without reprovisioning or server restart:

| Command | Who can call | What it does |
|---------|-------------|--------------|
| `nvflare study register` | `project_admin`, `org_admin` | Register a
new study with initial site enrollment |
| `nvflare study show` | any enrolled user | Show study definition
(site-orgs, users) |
| `nvflare study list` | any enrolled user | List studies visible to the
caller |
| `nvflare study remove` | `project_admin` | Remove a study (blocked if
jobs exist) |
| `nvflare study add-site` | `project_admin`, `org_admin` | Enroll
additional sites |
| `nvflare study remove-site` | `project_admin`, `org_admin` | Remove
sites from a study |
| `nvflare study add-user` | `project_admin`, org-enrolled `org_admin` |
Add a user to a study's admin list |
| `nvflare study remove-user` | `project_admin`, org-enrolled
`org_admin` | Remove a user from a study's admin list |

`project_admin` specifies sites grouped by org with `--site-org
<org>:<site>`.
`org_admin` specifies only their own org's sites with `--sites`.

All commands return a structured JSON envelope (`--format json`) or
human-readable text.
Changes take effect immediately via hot-reload — no server restart
required.

## Design Approach and Key Design Decisions

### 1. Two-layer INVALID_ARGS enforcement

The role-based input-shape contract (`project_admin` uses `--site-org`,
`org_admin` uses `--sites`)
is enforced at two independent layers:

- **CLI fast-fail** — `_try_get_caller_role()` reads the caller's role
from their startup-kit
certificate before opening a server connection. Mis-shaped commands are
rejected immediately
  with a structured `INVALID_ARGS` error, before any network round-trip.
- **Server authoritative** — `_requested_site_orgs()` re-checks
`ConnProps.USER_ROLE` on every
mutation. The CLI layer is advisory; the server always has the final
word. This ensures
  correctness even if the CLI is bypassed or the cert is stale.

### 2. Atomic mutation with registry validation

All mutations follow a strict sequence:

```
acquire lock → load JSON → deepcopy → apply callback → validate via
StudyRegistry constructor → atomic write (tempfile rename) →
publish to StudyRegistryService → release lock in finally
```

The `StudyRegistry` constructor is the single validation gate —
duplicate-site detection,
naming rules, and structure checks all live there. An invalid callback
result is rejected
before the write is attempted, preserving consistency.

### 3. Study visibility scoping

`list_studies` and `show_study` visibility mirrors the session
study-scoping model already
established for jobs: `project_admin` sees all studies; `org_admin` sees
studies in which
their org has enrolled at least one site.

### 4. SessionSpec completeness

All 8 study methods are declared as `@abstractmethod` on `SessionSpec`
so implementors get
compile-time guidance rather than runtime `AttributeError` surprises.

### 5. Security: empty-org guard

`_requested_site_orgs()` validates that `_caller_org(conn)` is non-empty
before using it as a
dict key. A misconfigured org_admin cert (empty ORG property) would
otherwise silently create
`{"": [sites]}` in the registry — now it raises `INVALID_ARGS` instead.

## Implementation

### New files
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `nvflare/private/fed/server/study_cmds.py` | Server-side
`StudyCmdModule` with 8 command handlers |
| `nvflare/tool/study/study_cli.py` | CLI command group: argparse →
FLARE API session calls |
| `docs/user_guide/nvflare_cli/study_command.rst` | User guide for the
study command family |
| `docs/design/participant_registration.md` | Design doc for participant
registration flow |
| `tests/unit_test/private/fed/server/study_cmds_test.py` | 63
server-side unit tests |
| `tests/unit_test/tool/study/study_cli_test.py` | 30 CLI-layer unit
tests |

### Modified files
- `nvflare/security/study_registry.py` — duplicate-site detection,
flat-site union derivation
- `nvflare/fuel/flare_api/api_spec.py` — 8 `@abstractmethod`
declarations on `SessionSpec`
- `nvflare/fuel/flare_api/flare_api.py` — concrete implementations for
all 8 study session methods
- `nvflare/cli.py` — study command group registered
- `nvflare/tool/cli_errors.py` — shared structured error output helpers
- `nvflare/apis/fl_constant.py`, `client.py`, `utils/format_check.py` —
study name constants and validation
- `nvflare/lighter/provision.py` — `study_registry.json` generation from
`project.yml`
- `nvflare/private/fed/server/client_manager.py`, `cmd_utils.py`,
`server_cmd_modules.py` — study-scoped client visibility and command
module registration
- `nvflare/fuel/hci/server/login.py` — study login integration
- `nvflare/private/fed/utils/identity_utils.py` — cert-to-identity
helpers used by CLI role resolution
- Design docs (`multistudy.md`, `multistudy_cli.md`) — two-layer
enforcement section, Phase 2 dataset-mapping content removed
- `docs/user_guide/admin_guide/multi_study_guide.rst` — cross-reference
to runtime study management guide

### Test coverage (93 unit tests)
- All 8 command handlers (register, show, list, remove, add-site,
remove-site, add-user, remove-user)

CLI-side tests)

- Lock timeout path
- User membership visibility scoping
- Duplicate-site rejection in StudyRegistry
- CLI golden paths and error-envelope mapping

subject: Fix Flare API multi-target command round-trip quoting (#4460)
message:
Fix Flare API multi-target command round-trip quoting (#4460)

Summary:
Several Flare API methods on the Session class —
Session.get_client_job_status(client_names=[...]),
Session.check_status(target_type='client', targets=[...]), and the
_collect_info helper (used by show_stats / show_errors) — raised
InvalidTarget('invalid client(s): ...') whenever more than one target
name was supplied, even when every name was a registered client.
Single-target calls worked, which hid the bug from existing unit tests.

Root cause: 
process_targets_into_str(targets) space-joins the names into one string;
join_args(parts) then wraps that single-element-with-whitespace in
double quotes; server-side parse_command_line sees the quotes and uses
shlex.split, which preserves the quoted content as one token;
validate_command_targets receives a one-element list (e.g. ['site-1
site-2']) and the name lookup falls through to INVALID_TARGET.

Fix: 
append each target name as its own element of parts via
parts.extend(targets); keep process_targets_into_str(targets) as a
validation-only call so SyntaxError is still raised for malformed
inputs.

Added multi-target regression tests for check_status,
get_client_job_status, show_stats, show_errors (4 new tests; all 54
existing tests still pass).

Background:
This bug has been present in NVFlare for a long time — specifically,
since the parse_command_line shlex path was added in July 2024 (PR
#2647). It went undetected because the QA test scripts had special-case
handling that happened to bypass the broken code path. When QA recently
refactored those test scripts, the special-case handling was removed and
the latent bug surfaced.

Changes:
nvflare/fuel/flare_api/flare_api.py — 3 call sites changed
(get_client_job_status, check_status, _collect_info — the latter
is used by show_stats / show_errors).

tests/unit_test/fuel/flare_api/session_new_methods_test.py — 4 new
multi-target regression tests.

subject: Enhance NVFlare CLI startup kit workflows (#4479)
message:
Enhance NVFlare CLI startup kit workflows (#4479)

## Summary

- Add a local startup kit registry with the new `nvflare config kit`
command so server-connected commands use one active kit instead of
repeated `--startup-target` / `--startup-kit` arguments.
- Route `nvflare job`, `nvflare study`, and `nvflare system` through
shared active-kit session resolution, with `NVFLARE_STARTUP_KIT_DIR`
kept as the automation override.
- Update POC workflows so `poc prepare` and `poc add user` register
generated admin/user startup kits in `~/.nvflare/config.conf`; `poc add
site` provisions a site kit but does not register it as an active CLI
identity.
- Add project-admin validation before `poc add user` / `poc add site`
mutate local POC metadata.
- Improve `nvflare config` migration behavior by backing up
`config.conf` and warning when old startup-kit keys such as
`poc.startup_kit` or `prod.startup_kit` are stripped.
- Expand `nvflare job logs` to read server-side stored logs, including
client logs already streamed to the server, with human-readable default
output and JSON support.
- Update CLI user guides, migration notes, and the consolidated CLI
design doc to match the implemented behavior.

## Details

### Startup kit registry

- Adds `nvflare/tool/kit` with `add`, `use`, `show`, `list`, and
`remove` handlers under `nvflare config kit`.
- Stores local kit registrations under `startup_kits.entries` and active
selection under `startup_kits.active`.
- Supports admin/user kits for active command sessions.
- Rejects site/server kits through `nvflare config kit add`; if manually
edited or migrated config contains stale non-admin entries, `kit list`
shows them so users can remove them.
- Keeps startup-kit path management out of the root `nvflare config`
options.

### POC workflow

- `poc prepare` registers generated project admin, org admin, lead, and
other admin/user startup kits. Site startup kits are not registered
because they are service identities, not CLI user identities.
- `poc add user` persists local POC project metadata, reuses the
existing POC provisioning state, registers the generated user kit, and
preserves the active kit unless no active kit exists.
- `poc add site` persists the new client participant and generates the
site startup kit, but does not register the site kit in the active
startup-kit registry.
- `poc clean` removes POC-generated registry entries using canonical
workspace path matching.

### Job logs

- Removes `--tail` and `--grep` from `nvflare job logs`.
- Defaults to server logs and supports `--site server`, `--site
<client>`, and `--site all`.
- Keeps `Session.get_job_logs(..., tail_lines=..., grep_pattern=...)`
compatibility for Python callers by filtering locally in the session
wrapper.
- Reads live server workspace logs first, then stored job workspace
artifacts.
